what_is_working.text: On target this period: Median first-response time (business hours); Be-backs vs fresh-ups balance; Leads unassigned past 2 hours; Unfilled personalization tags in messages.

largest_controllable_opportunity.text: Appointment no-show rate (Appointment conversion) is the largest controllable opportunity, weighing off-target severity, three-store peer position, and evidence confidence.

how_evidence_connects.text: A healthy median response time sits alongside leads with no tracked response within the first 30 minutes and a below-target set rate: fast average speed is not translating into set appointments while some leads get no tracked response in the first 30 minutes.

executive_narrative.claim_layers_legend: fact = a measured value; inference = a bounded reading of the cited measurements; hypothesis = a testable explanation needing more evidence; recommendation = an action.

facts.label: Median first-response time (business hours)

industry_reference.note: shown for context only; not used to score this metric

facts.text: Median first-response time (business hours): 4.5 min (target at or below 10 min; on target; middle of the three rooftops).

facts.label: Leads with no tracked response within 30 minutes
facts.text: Leads with no tracked response within 30 minutes: 3.1% (target at or below 0%; off target; strongest of the three rooftops).

facts.label: Rep first-response outliers vs the store median
facts.text: Rep first-response outliers vs the store median: 66.7% (target at or below 0%; off target; middle of the three rooftops).

narrative.text: The store-average first-response time is 4.5 min, which reads on target — but that average hides inconsistency: 3.1% of business-hours leads had no tracked response within the first 30 minutes and rep first-response outliers are off target. A healthy median can coexist with leads that get no tracked response within the first 30 minutes, so average speed alone overstates coverage.

implication.text: Coaching to the store average would miss the real gap; the opportunity is even coverage of every lead, not a faster headline median.

hypotheses.text: Leads with no tracked response in the first 30 minutes may concentrate in specific hours, sources, or individual reps rather than being spread evenly; a per-rep/per-hour view would confirm.

actions.action: Stand up a daily sweep of leads with no tracked response yet, so no business-hours lead passes 30 minutes without a tracked first response.

facts.label: Templated messages with no personalization
facts.text: Templated messages with no personalization: 12.5% (target at or below 0%; off target; strongest of the three rooftops).

facts.label: Text-vs-call balance (voice avoidance)
facts.text: Text-vs-call balance (voice avoidance): 28.6% (target at or below 0%; off target; middle of the three rooftops).

facts.label: Customers sending 2+ messages before a reply
facts.text: Customers sending 2+ messages before a reply: 1.7% (target at or below 0%; off target; strongest of the three rooftops).

facts.label: Unfilled personalization tags in messages
facts.text: Unfilled personalization tags in messages: 0% (target at or below 0%; on target; strongest of the three rooftops).

facts.label: Same message reused across many customers
facts.text: Same message reused across many customers: 0.4% (target at or below 0%; off target; weakest of the three rooftops).

facts.label: Very short, low-effort replies
facts.text: Very short, low-effort replies: 0% (target at or below 0%; on target; strongest of the three rooftops).

facts.label: Link-only replies with no context
facts.text: Link-only replies with no context: 0% (target at or below 0%; on target; strongest of the three rooftops).

narrative.text: Messaging quality shows 4 flagged behaviors this period — Templated messages with no personalization, Text-vs-call balance (voice avoidance), Customers sending 2+ messages before a reply, Same message reused across many customers. These are observed message patterns, not proven intent; taken together they point toward template reliance and low-effort or one-way replies.

implication.text: Two or more messaging flags together suggest reps lean on templates and text over personalized, two-way conversation — a coachable quality gap, not a volume gap.

hypotheses.text: Template reliance may be driven by workload or CRM shortcuts rather than skill; a short message-quality review with reps would separate cause from symptom.

actions.action: Run a weekly message-quality review: personalize the opening, balance text with a call attempt, and replace link-only replies with a question.
actions.success_measure: flagged messaging behaviors trending down week over week

facts.label: Lead-to-appointment set rate

industry_reference.note: shown for context only; not used to score this metric

facts.text: Lead-to-appointment set rate: 15.8% (target at or above 25%; off target; strongest of the three rooftops).

facts.label: Appointment show rate

industry_reference.note: shown for context only; not used to score this metric

facts.text: Appointment show rate: 42.9% (target at or above 55%; off target; middle of the three rooftops).

facts.label: Show-to-write rate
facts.text: Show-to-write rate: 0% (target at or above 60%; off target; strongest of the three rooftops).

facts.label: Appointment no-show rate
facts.text: Appointment no-show rate: 57.1% (target at or below 45%; off target; weakest of the three rooftops).

narrative.text: Across the appointment funnel this period: lead-to-set is 15.8% (off target, target 25%+), show rate is 42.9% (off target), no-show rate is 57.1% (off target), and show-to-write is 0% (off target). The show rate is measured over every appointment row this period (its accepted formula counts shows over all appointment rows), so it is not the same denominator as an industry appointments-set benchmark.

implication.text: The largest controllable step here is getting more leads to a set appointment; show and write cannot compound on appointments that were never set.

hypotheses.text: A low set rate can reflect customer follow-through, appointment-request quality, the confirmation process, or CRM logging of set appointments; these are distinct causes and none is established without a per-appointment review.
A weak show or high no-show rate may reflect confirmation cadence rather than lead quality; a confirmation-call audit would separate them.

actions.action: Tighten the set-and-confirm routine: a same-day appointment ask on every worked lead and a confirmation touch the day before.
actions.success_measure: lead-to-set rate moving toward the 25% target and no-show rate falling

facts.label: Be-backs vs fresh-ups balance
facts.text: Be-backs vs fresh-ups balance: 27.3% (target at or below 100%; on target; weakest of the three rooftops).

facts.label: Test-drive completion rate
facts.text: Test-drive completion rate: 0% (target at or above 50%; off target; middle of the three rooftops).

facts.label: Leads unassigned past 2 hours
facts.text: Leads unassigned past 2 hours: 0% (target at or below 0%; on target; strongest of the three rooftops).

narrative.text: Showroom execution this period: be-backs vs fresh-ups is 27.3% (on target), test-drive completion is 0% (off target), and lead assignment past 2 hours is 0% (on target). A zero test-drive value may reflect logging rather than activity — it does not prove no test-drives happened.

implication.text: Assignment timeliness passed this specific two-hour check this period; later ownership and execution quality remain separate questions this report does not measure, so a soft follow-through signal is not attributed to any single cause here.

hypotheses.text: A low or zero test-drive value may be a CRM logging habit rather than missing showroom follow-through; confirm against the showroom log before drawing a performance conclusion.

actions.action: Confirm test-drive and visit logging discipline at the desk, then coach to complete a test-drive on every showroom visit.
actions.success_measure: test-drive completion rising and logged consistently

cross_cluster_synthesis.text: A healthy median response time sits alongside leads with no tracked response within the first 30 minutes and a below-target set rate: fast average speed is not translating into set appointments while some leads get no tracked response in the first 30 minutes.
A below-target set rate and a soft show rate coincide with a messaging-quality flag, suggesting the appointment gap is partly a conversation-quality gap, not only volume.

Assignment timeliness passed its two-hour check while showroom follow-through is soft. One hypothesis worth testing is that the opportunity lies in execution after assignment; this does not rule out assignment quality, which the two-hour check does not measure.
